observed_reality: Frank central state code uses Python sqlite3 and WAL without an exact loaded-runtime identity gate before canonical database opens.
The self-hosted Ubuntu lane runner clay on host digital-retina executes /usr/bin/python3 with SQLite 3.45.1 on the measured baseline path.
The baseline loaded libsqlite3 artifact is /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libsqlite3.so.0.8.6 with SHA-256 f2cd05de8b6f71ea9d0495a6f9ff9cae844b15d9c45b7ef49ee0af0f81658cc7.
A disposable rootless build of official SQLite 3.53.4 was loaded by the same /usr/bin/python3 with the expected source ID and without opening a Frank database.

Fresh main independently proved that V4 can admit two distinct internally self-consistent SQLite 3.53.4 builds when the caller supplies the matching manifest digest; caller-selected consistency is not an independent deployment trust anchor.
V5 candidate removes caller-selected SQLite identity arguments and binds admission to a fixed root-owned deployment anchor candidate at /opt/frank-v0.1/sqlite-runtime-v1.
On the self-hosted target lane V5 passed deterministic gates and failed closed with exit 78 before target execution when the fixed deployment anchor was absent.
A full ephemeral root-owned anchor E2E attempt was blocked at sudo -n true because the runner requires a sudo password; this occurred before any /opt mutation or Frank database open.
grf.hypothesis: Release-safe WAL persistence requires both exact active-library attestation and an independently authorized deployment trust anchor that a process caller cannot choose.
grf.strongest_counterhypothesis: A caller-supplied manifest digest plus internal artifact consistency is sufficient to establish the authorized SQLite runtime identity.
grf.collapse: The strongest counterhypothesis is refuted by the fresh-main two-build counterworld. V5 closes the caller-selection interface in candidate code and proves fail-closed behavior without an anchor, but independent privileged anchor provisioning is not available from the current GitHub Actions runner capability.

upstream_evidence.sqlite_wal_reset_affected: 3.7.0 through 3.51.2 under documented concurrent writer/checkpoint conditions

parallel_worker_fusion.interpretation: V4 proves consistency with caller-supplied digest, not independent authorization of which digest/runtime is allowed.

v5_candidate.anchor_policy: absolute fixed path; non-symlink; UID 0; not group/world writable; manifest digest read without following symlinks

privileged_anchor_e2e.interpretation: Current self-hosted Actions lane lacks noninteractive admin capability needed to establish the proposed root-owned independent deployment anchor. Do not weaken the anchor merely to make CI pass.

negative_results.result: A good CLI/package version cannot establish the library identity loaded by Python.
The measured baseline /usr/bin/python3 path loads SQLite 3.45.1, not 3.53.4.
Two distinct 3.53.4 artifacts can both pass V4 when the caller supplies the corresponding self-consistent manifest digest.
The current self-hosted GitHub Actions runner cannot noninteractively provision a root-owned trust anchor because sudo requires a password.

unusual_experiment.description: A temporary fake sqlite3 CLI reported 3.53.4 while Python in the same environment reported its actually loaded SQLite 3.46.1; the temporary decoy was deleted immediately after measurement.
unusual_experiment.purpose: Falsify package/CLI-version evidence as a sufficient release signal.

release_adjudication.reason: The accepted-lane baseline Python runtime is still SQLite 3.45.1. V4 has an independently measured caller-selected trust-anchor gap. V5 closes that interface in candidate code and fails closed without the fixed anchor, but the current CI lane cannot provision the root-owned independent anchor for end-to-end production-path proof.
release_adjudication.next_smallest_falsifier: Use an independently authorized deployment/admin lane to provision the approved fixed SQLite bundle at the accepted trust anchor, then prove V5 exact-target admission plus downgrade/library-swap rejection and non-bypassable service/bootstrap routing before any canonical WAL DB open. If privileged provisioning is intentionally unavailable, canonically choose and test an equivalently independent trust anchor rather than caller-selected input.
promotion_forbidden_until: fixed productive runtime is installed or otherwise independently bound
independent trust-anchor authority is proven and not caller/model/Frank selectable
exact runtime/source/artifact identity is fail-closed before canonical WAL database opens
downgrade/library-swap and bypass rejection are tested
